correctness.rationale: Every subdivision signature is the selected original-endpoint intersection, forcing all but at most one original vertex into a code. Original signatures are distinct exactly when the selected-edge graph has at most one isolated vertex and no K2 components; closed domination requires an isolated original to be selected. This proves disjoint all-set polynomial decompositions; inclusion-exclusion counts the selected-edge graphs; tree-component edge bounds and Cayley enumeration prove minima and optimizer counts. A separate adjacency-based direct verifier exhaustively checks 2,131,008 candidate subsets and nine symbolic orders.

value.rationale: The result gives complete OD and OTD code-cardinality distributions and exact minimum optimizer counts for a natural infinite family of incidence graphs. It resolves the general one-unit OD-versus-OTD ambiguity by a sharp residue-class law and explains it through allowed isolated original vertices and maximum-component spanning forests. The explicit family-wide structure is more than a routine bound specialization.
